    Each request the node sends stops after 30 seconds, even when the node timeout is longer or not set. A response body larger than 10 MiB, the default limit an administrator can change, fails the node without a retry.

    - Execution configuration

    Set the Execution mode to control how the node behaves when several branches converge on it.

    Mode Behavior Execute once per branch The node runs once for each incoming branch. Applies when this section isn't configured. Wait for all branches The node waits for all incoming branches to complete, then runs once.

Execution outputs

When executed, the node returns the following outputs. Each output is a JSON value:

Output Type Description body object The response body returned by Microsoft Graph. code number The HTTP status code returned by Microsoft Graph. headers object The response headers returned by Microsoft Graph.

To access outputs, select your Microsoft Entra ID node and then select in the top-right corner of the screen. Hover over each output name to view its details.

You can then reuse these outputs as output variables in subsequent nodes. Select the $var button, or enter $ and select the output from the suggestions. Inserted references appear in the following form:

  • $<node_name>.body.<field_name>: to get a value from the response body, for example a user's object ID
  • $<node_name>.code: to get the HTTP status code, for example to check whether the request succeeded
  • $<node_name>.headers.<header_name>: to get a specific response header

docs.title: Configure a Jira Cloud integration node
docs.text:
A Jira Cloud integration node runs operations against the Jira Cloud platform REST API v3. It can create, edit, transition, link, and delete issues, and search issues with Jira Query Language (JQL). It can also manage comments, attachments, worklogs, watchers, and votes, and browse projects, issue types, priorities, and resolutions. Each operation is a dedicated action selected within the node.

  1. Go to the Flow view from the sidebar menu.

  2. Select a workflow from the list.

  3. Drag the previous node connector to an empty area of the canvas.

  4. In the What is the next step? drawer, select Integrations.

  5. Select Jira Cloud.

  6. In the Jira Cloud drawer, enter the following information:

    Insert a variable with the $var button, or enter $ and select a variable from the suggestions. To access a field, select the variable to edit its jq expression, or use the + button to insert the variable and the field together.

    • $<node_name>.body.results[0].id: Reads the first identifier of an API response.
    • $<node_name>.body.items | map(.name) | join(", "): Turns a list of objects into a comma-separated text.
    • $<node_name>.body.createdAt / 1000 | todate: Formats a TheHive date, a Unix timestamp in milliseconds, as an ISO 8601 date.

    The URL of your Jira Cloud site: https://<site_name>.atlassian.net.

    - Authentication *

    In the Authentication section, select the Authentication method and provide its credentials. The Jira Cloud node supports two methods:

    Authentication method Fields basic_auth Username *, Password bearer_token Bearer token *

    With basic_auth, the username is the Atlassian account email and the password is an Atlassian API token. Use bearer_token with an OAuth 2.0 access token.

    - Headers

    Extra headers added to every request sent by the node. Select to add a header key and its value.

    Header values are stored in plaintext

    Header values appear in plaintext in the workflow execution history. Reference a secret global variable instead of pasting a credential directly.

    - Action *

    The operation to perform in Jira. Available actions:

    Family Actions Issues Create Issue, Get Issue, Edit Issue, Transition Issue, Get Transitions, Assign Issue, Bulk Create Issues, Bulk Fetch Issues, Delete Issue Issue Search Search Issues (JQL), Search Issues (JQL POST), Count Issues, Match Issues to JQL, Parse JQL Queries, Get Issue Picker Suggestions Issue Comments Add Comment, Get Comments, Get Comment, Update Comment, Get Comments by IDs, Delete Comment Issue Attachments Get Attachment Metadata, Get Attachment Content, Get Attachment Settings, Get Attachment Thumbnail, Expand Attachment for Humans, Expand Attachment for Machines, Delete Attachment Issue Links Create Issue Link, Get Issue Link Types, Get Issue Link Type, Get Issue Link, Delete Issue Link Issue Remote Links Create or Update Remote Issue Link, Get Remote Issue Links, Get Remote Issue Link, Update Remote Issue Link, Delete Remote Issue Link, Delete Remote Issue Link by Global ID Issue Watchers Notify Issue, Get Issue Watchers, Remove Watcher, Get Is Watching Issue Bulk Issue History Get Changelogs, Bulk Fetch Changelogs, Get Changelogs by IDs Issue Metadata Get Create Issue Metadata, Get Create Issue Metadata Issue Types, Get Create Issue Metadata Issue Type, Get Edit Issue Metadata, Get Events Issue Types Get Issue Types, Get Issue Type, Get Issue Types for Project Issue Priorities Get Priorities, Get Priority, Search Priorities Issue Resolutions Get Resolutions, Get Resolution, Search Resolutions Issue Worklogs Add Worklog, Get Issue Worklogs, Update Worklog, Delete Worklog Issue Votes Get Votes, Add Vote, Remove Vote Projects Get All Projects, Search Projects, Get Project, Get Project Statuses, Get Project Versions, Get Project Components User Search Find Users, Find Assignable Users Tasks Get Task, Cancel Task

    - Editor mode

    For actions that send a request body, select how to provide it:

    Query parameters sent with the request, entered as key-value pairs. Select to add a parameter. This section appears only for actions that accept query parameters.

docs.text:
Beta

A Microsoft Teams integration node runs operations against the Microsoft Graph API. It can send, reply to, update, and delete channel messages, send chat messages, and create chats and channels. It can also add team and channel members, and list or retrieve teams, channels, chats, messages, and replies. Each operation is a dedicated action selected within the node.

  2. Select a workflow from the list.

  3. Drag the previous node connector to an empty area of the canvas.

  4. In the What is the next step? drawer, select Integrations.

  5. Select Microsoft Teams.

  6. In the Microsoft Teams drawer, enter the following information:

    Variables

    • $<node_name>.output.title | ascii_upcase: Converts a text to uppercase.

    Fields marked with * are mandatory.

    - Base URL *

    The URL of Microsoft Graph: https://graph.microsoft.com. The node targets the v1.0 version of Microsoft Graph.

    - Authentication *

    Authentication method Fields oauth2 Access token, Client ID, Client secret, Refresh token, Token URL. Authorization URL and Token scopes have no effect oauth2_client_credentials Client ID *, Client secret *, Token URL *, Token scopes

    Both methods use the token URL of your Microsoft Entra ID tenant, https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token. oauth2 acts on behalf of a user, typically a service account. oauth2_client_credentials fetches an application token with the client ID and secret: set its token scope to https://graph.microsoft.com/.default. Reference secret global variables instead of pasting credentials directly.

    With oauth2, fill in the fields of one of the two cases:

    Field With an access token With a refresh token Example Client ID Not used Required $global.teams_client_id Client secret Not used Optional, for a confidential client $secret.teams_client_secret Access token Required Not used $secret.teams_access_token Refresh token Not used Required $secret.teams_refresh_token Token URL Not used Required https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant>/oauth2/v2.0/token

    The node sends an access token as is and never renews it: once it expires, calls fail until it's replaced, so it suits a quick test. A refresh token suits a workflow that runs over time: each step execution gets a fresh access token from it. Microsoft Entra ID issues a refresh token only when the application requests the offline_access scope at sign-in.

    Sending messages requires the oauth2 method

    Microsoft Graph doesn't let an application post messages on its own behalf. The Send Channel Message, Reply to Channel Message, Update Channel Message, Delete Channel Message, and Send Chat Message actions fail with oauth2_client_credentials. Use the oauth2 method for them. The node then posts messages as the user the tokens belong to. All other actions work with both methods.

    Prerequisite

    Grant the application the Microsoft Graph permissions matching the actions and the authentication method you use: delegated permissions for oauth2, application permissions for oauth2_client_credentials.     - Headers

    Extra headers added to every request sent by the node. Select to add a header key and its value.

    Header values are stored in plaintext

    Header values appear in plaintext in the workflow execution history. Reference a secret global variable instead of pasting a credential directly.

    - Action *

    The operation to perform in Microsoft Teams. Available actions:

    Family Actions Messages Send Channel Message, Reply to Channel Message, Update Channel Message, Delete Channel Message, Get Channel Message, List Channel Messages, List Message Replies Chats Send Chat Message, Create Chat, List Chats Teams & Channels List Joined Teams, Get Team, List Channels, Get Channel, Create Channel, Add Channel Member, Add Team Member

    After you select an action, the drawer displays the fields specific to that action. For the meaning and format of each field, see the Microsoft Graph API documentation.

    Identifying teams, channels, and chats

    Actions take the identifiers Microsoft Graph uses, not display names. The Team ID field takes the ID of the team's Microsoft 365 group, and the Channel ID and Chat ID fields take identifiers starting with 19:. To find them, use List Joined Teams with a user's object ID or user principal name, then List Channels or List Chats. The User ID and User fields accept either the object ID or the user principal name of a user.

    Message body format

    The Message body field takes a JSON object with the contentType and content of the message, for example {"contentType": "html", "content": "<b>New alert</b> raised in TheHive"}. Set contentType to text for plain text or html to format the message. To mention users, use html and add an <at id="0">Name</at> tag for each entry of the Mentions field. Delete Channel Message performs a soft delete.

    Adding members

    Create Chat, Create Channel, Add Channel Member, and Add Team Member describe each member with the Microsoft Graph member format:

    • The Member type field or the @odata.type property is #microsoft.graph.aadUserConversationMember
    • The User field or the user@odata.bind property is the Graph URL of the user, such as https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/users('jdoe@contoso.com')
    • Roles is ["owner"] for an owner or [] for a member

    Add Channel Member applies only to private and shared channels.

    • Raw: Provide the whole request body in the Request body (raw) field.

    Mode Behavior Execute once per branch The node runs once for each incoming branch. Applies when this section isn't configured. Wait for all branches The node waits for all incoming branches to complete, then runs once.

Execution outputs

When executed, the node returns the following outputs. Each output is a JSON value:

Output Type Description body object The response body returned by Microsoft Graph. code number The HTTP status code returned by Microsoft Graph. headers object The response headers returned by Microsoft Graph.

To access outputs, select your Microsoft Teams node and then select in the top-right corner of the screen. Hover over each output name to view its details.

You can then reuse these outputs as output variables in subsequent nodes. Select the $var button, or enter $ and select the output from the suggestions. Inserted references appear in the following form:

  • $<node_name>.body.<field_name>: to get a value from the response body, for example the id of the message returned by Send Channel Message, used to reply to, update, or delete the message or list its replies. Update Channel Message and Delete Channel Message return a 204 status code with an empty body.
  • $<node_name>.code: to get the HTTP status code, for example to check whether the request succeeded
  • $<node_name>.headers.<header_name>: to get a specific response header

docs.title: Configure a ServiceNow integration node
docs.text:
A ServiceNow integration node runs operations against the ServiceNow Table and Attachment APIs. It can create, retrieve, and update incidents and change requests, and search configuration items, users, and user groups. It can also manage record attachments, and read, create, update, and delete records in any table. Each operation is a dedicated action selected within the node.

  1. Go to the Flow view from the sidebar menu.

  2. Select a workflow from the list.

  3. Drag the previous node connector to an empty area of the canvas.

  4. In the What is the next step? drawer, select Integrations.

  5. Select ServiceNow.

  6. In the ServiceNow drawer, enter the following information:

    Variables

    Insert a variable with the $var button, or enter $ and select a variable from the suggestions. To access a field, select the variable to edit its jq expression, or use the + button to insert the variable and the field together.

    Inside the expression, jq functions transform the value before it's inserted in the field. The whole expression stays inside the blue reference, for example:

    • $<node_name>.body.results[0].id: Reads the first identifier of an API response.
    • $<node_name>.body.items | map(.name) | join(", "): Turns a list of objects into a comma-separated text.
    • $<node_name>.body.createdAt / 1000 | todate: Formats a TheHive date, a Unix timestamp in milliseconds, as an ISO 8601 date.
    • $<node_name>.output.title | ascii_upcase: Converts a text to uppercase.

    See Jq Functions for the full list of available functions.

    Fields marked with * are mandatory.

    - Base URL *

    The URL of your ServiceNow instance: https://<instance_name>.service-now.com.

    - Authentication *

    In the Authentication section, select the Authentication method and provide its credentials. The ServiceNow node supports four methods:

    Authentication method Fields basic_auth Username *, Password bearer_token Bearer token * oauth2 Access token, Client ID, Client secret, Refresh token, Token URL. Authorization URL and Token scopes have no effect oauth2_client_credentials Client ID *, Client secret *, Token URL *, Token scopes

    With basic_auth, provide the credentials of a ServiceNow user whose roles cover the tables the actions use. With bearer_token, provide an OAuth 2.0 access token obtained outside the workflow. The two OAuth 2.0 methods authenticate with an OAuth API client registered in ServiceNow, and their token URL is https://<instance_name>.service-now.com/oauth_token.do. oauth2_client_credentials fetches the token with the client ID and secret. Reference secret global variables instead of pasting credentials directly.

    With oauth2, fill in the fields of one of the two cases:

    Field With an access token With a refresh token Example Client ID Not used Required $global.servicenow_client_id Client secret Not used Optional, for a confidential client $secret.servicenow_client_secret Access token Required Not used $secret.servicenow_access_token Refresh token Not used Required $secret.servicenow_refresh_token Token URL Not used Required https://<instance_name>.service-now.com/oauth_token.do

    The node sends an access token as is and never renews it: once it expires, calls fail until it's replaced, so it suits a quick test. A refresh token suits a workflow that runs over time: each step execution gets a fresh access token from it. ServiceNow returns a refresh token with the access token, and the OAuth API client registered in ServiceNow sets how long it stays valid.

    - Headers

    Extra headers added to every request sent by the node. Select to add a header key and its value.

    Header values are stored in plaintext

    Header values appear in plaintext in the workflow execution history. Reference a secret global variable instead of pasting a credential directly.

    - Action *

    The operation to perform in ServiceNow. Available actions:

    Family Actions Incidents List Incidents, Get Incident, Create Incident, Update Incident Change Requests List Change Requests, Get Change Request, Create Change Request, Update Change Request CMDB Search Configuration Item, Get Configuration Item Users & Groups Search User, Search User Group Attachments List Attachments, Get Attachment, Add Attachment, Delete Attachment Custom Tables List Records, Get Record, Create Record, Replace Record, Update Record, Delete Record

    After you select an action, the drawer displays the fields specific to that action. For the meaning and format of each field, see the ServiceNow REST API documentation.

    Records are addressed by sys_id

    The get, update, replace, and delete actions identify a record by its sys_id, a 32-character identifier, not by its number such as INC0010001. To resolve a number to a sys_id, use the matching list or search action with an encoded query. In Query parameters, add a parameter named sysparm_query with a value such as number=INC0010001. Encoded queries chain conditions with ^ and sort with ORDERBY or ORDERBYDESC, for example active=true^urgency=1^ORDERBYDESCsys_created_on.

    The Custom Tables actions

    The Custom Tables actions read and write any ServiceNow table by its name, such as sc_request, including custom tables. Their write actions take the record fields as a single Fields field holding a JSON object, sent verbatim as the request body, for example {"short_description": "Ransomware detected on FIN-DB-01", "urgency": "1"}.

    The Add Attachment action

    Add Attachment attaches a file to a record. The File field takes a file reference produced by an earlier node, such as a file downloaded by an HTTP request action node or uploaded to the Webhook trigger, not literal text content. The field holds one reference and nothing else. Text around the reference or a second reference shows an inline error, because the run would fail. In this field, picking an entry from the Files group of the variable suggestions inserts the file itself, not its metadata.

    - Editor mode

    For actions that send a request body, select how to provide it:

    • Form: Fill in one field per body parameter.
    • Raw: Provide the whole request body in the Request body (raw) field.

    - Query parameters

    Query parameters sent with the request, entered as key-value pairs. Select to add a parameter. This section appears only for actions that accept query parameters.

    The following actions require query parameters. Add each one with the name listed, or the node fails:

    • Search Configuration Item: sysparm_query
    • Search User: sysparm_query
    • Search User Group: sysparm_query

  7. Optional: Configure the following settings.

    - Proxy

    Configure how the node connects to the external service when a proxy is required.

    Select a Proxy mode:

    • Do not use a proxy: No proxy is applied. All requests are sent directly. This is the default.

    • Use the platform default proxy configuration: Uses the global proxy settings defined in TheHive application.conf. See proxy configuration in TheHive.

    • Configure a custom proxy: Defines a custom proxy for this node, overriding the global configuration.

    When Proxy mode is Configure a custom proxy, provide the following information:

    Field Example Protocol https Address * proxy.example.com Port 8080 Username $global.proxy_user Password $secret.proxy_password

    - SSL/TLS

    Configure SSL/TLS settings for secure communication with the external service.

    Use this section when the service relies on a private certificate authority (CA), requires client certificate authentication through mutual TLS, or uses a non-standard trust chain.

    Field Description Client certificate (mTLS) Whether the node authenticates with a client certificate (mutual TLS). Do not use a client certificate is the default. Select Provide a client certificate and key to fill in the two fields below. Client certificate (PEM) The client certificate to present during the SSL/TLS handshake, in PEM format. Required when Client certificate (mTLS) is Provide a client certificate and key. Client certificate key (PEM) The private key associated with the client certificate, in PEM format. Required when Client certificate (mTLS) is Provide a client certificate and key. Server verification How the node verifies the identity of the server. Uses the system's pre-installed certificate authorities is the default. Provide a custom CA certificate to verify the server uses the certificate in the next field. Do not verify the server's identity (not recommended for production) exposes the connection to security risks. CA certificate (PEM) The CA certificate used to verify the identity of the server, in PEM format. Required when Server verification is set to Provide a custom CA certificate to verify the server.

    - Error handling

    Configure whether the node fails on error responses.

    By default, the node fails when the response returns a 4xx or 5xx error status code. Turn on Ignore error status codes to make the node succeed regardless of the response status code. Then handle errors in the workflow, for example with an If flow node evaluating the code output. Error responses aren't retried when the option is on.

    Two cases still fail the node:

    • A transport failure, such as a DNS, connection, TLS, or timeout error. The node sets no output.
    • A response announced as JSON that can't be parsed. The node sets the code and headers outputs but no body, and isn't retried.

    When Ignore error status codes is off, the node retries a 408, 429, or 5xx response up to the number of times set in Retry attempts. Any other 4xx response fails the node immediately, without retrying. When the called service includes a Retry-After header in its response, the node waits that long before the next attempt, up to a maximum of 5 minutes. This wait replaces the delay set by Retry delay and Backoff.

  8. Optional: Select Add options to configure the following settings.

    - Timeout & retry

    Configure how the node handles execution time limits and failure recovery.

    If the timeout is reached, the node fails.

    Global timeout vs. local timeout

    A timeout for the entire workflow is defined when creating the workflow. When both a node timeout and a workflow-level timeout are defined, the shortest timeout value applies.

    Field Description Timeout Maximum allowed execution time for the node, in seconds, minutes, or hours. The minimum value is 30 seconds. Retry attempts Number of times the node is retried on failure. Retry delay Time to wait between retry attempts, in seconds, minutes, or hours. Without a delay, retries run 1 second apart by default. Backoff Coefficient applied to the retry delay to increase the wait time after each failed attempt.

    Retries and timeouts

    If the node includes retry settings, the timeout applies to each attempt, not to the total duration of all attempts.

    Each request the node sends stops after 30 seconds, even when the node timeout is longer or not set. A response body larger than 10 MiB, the default limit an administrator can change, fails the node without a retry.

    - Execution configuration

    Set the Execution mode to control how the node behaves when several branches converge on it.

    Mode Behavior Execute once per branch The node runs once for each incoming branch. Applies when this section isn't configured. Wait for all branches The node waits for all incoming branches to complete, then runs once.

Execution outputs

When executed, the node returns the following outputs. Each output is a JSON value:

Output Type Description body object The response body returned by ServiceNow. code number The HTTP status code returned by ServiceNow. headers object The response headers returned by ServiceNow.

To access outputs, select your ServiceNow node and then select in the top-right corner of the screen. Hover over each output name to view its details.

You can then reuse these outputs as output variables in subsequent nodes. Select the $var button, or enter $ and select the output from the suggestions. Inserted references appear in the following form:

  • $<node_name>.body.<field_name>: to get a value from the response body. ServiceNow wraps the response in a result field, for example $<node_name>.body.result.sys_id for the identifier of a created incident.
  • $<node_name>.code: to get the HTTP status code, for example to check whether the request succeeded
  • $<node_name>.headers.<header_name>: to get a specific response header

docs.title: Configure an OpenCTI integration node
docs.text:
An OpenCTI integration node runs operations against the OpenCTI GraphQL and TAXII 2.1 APIs. It can search entities, observables, indicators, and relationships, and create observables, indicators, reports, incidents, incident response cases, relationships, and sightings. It can also manage labels, markings, and notes, request enrichment from connectors, and read STIX objects through TAXII. Each operation is a dedicated action selected within the node.

  1. Go to the Flow view from the sidebar menu.

  2. Select a workflow from the list.

  3. Drag the previous node connector to an empty area of the canvas.

  4. In the What is the next step? drawer, select Integrations.

  5. Select OpenCTI.

  6. In the OpenCTI drawer, enter the following information:

    Variables

    Insert a variable with the $var button, or enter $ and select a variable from the suggestions. To access a field, select the variable to edit its jq expression, or use the + button to insert the variable and the field together.

    Inside the expression, jq functions transform the value before it's inserted in the field. The whole expression stays inside the blue reference, for example:

    • $<node_name>.body.results[0].id: Reads the first identifier of an API response.
    • $<node_name>.body.items | map(.name) | join(", "): Turns a list of objects into a comma-separated text.
    • $<node_name>.body.createdAt / 1000 | todate: Formats a TheHive date, a Unix timestamp in milliseconds, as an ISO 8601 date.
    • $<node_name>.output.title | ascii_upcase: Converts a text to uppercase.

    See Jq Functions for the full list of available functions.

    Fields marked with * are mandatory.

    - Base URL *

    The root URL of your OpenCTI platform, for example https://opencti.example.com. Don't add /graphql: the node appends the path of each action.

    - Authentication *

    In the Authentication section, select bearer_token as the Authentication method, then enter the API key of an OpenCTI user in the Bearer token field. Users find their API key in Profile > API access in OpenCTI. Reference a secret global variable instead of pasting the key directly.

    - Headers

    Extra headers added to every request sent by the node. Select to add a header key and its value.

    Header values are stored in plaintext

    Header values appear in plaintext in the workflow execution history. Reference a secret global variable instead of pasting a credential directly.

    - Action *

    The operation to perform in OpenCTI. Available actions:

    Family Actions GraphQL Execute GraphQL Operation Search Search Entities, Search Observables, Search Indicators, Search Relationships Observables Get Observable, Create Observable, Update Observable Fields, Promote Observable to Indicator, Delete Observable Indicators Get Indicator, Create Indicator Entities Get Entity, Export Entity as STIX, Delete Entity Containers Create Report, Create Incident, Create Incident Response Case, Add Entity to Container Relationships Create Relationship, Create Sighting Labels & Markings List Labels, Create Label, Add Label to Entity, List Marking Definitions, Add Marking to Entity Notes Add Note to Entity Enrichment List Connectors, List Enrichment Connectors for Type, Ask Enrichment Schema Get Schema (SDL), Introspect Types, Get Relationship Mapping System Who Am I, Get Platform Info, Health Check TAXII 2.1 TAXII Discovery, TAXII API Root, TAXII List Collections, TAXII Get Collection, TAXII Get Objects, TAXII Get Object, TAXII Get Object Versions, TAXII Get Manifest

    After you select an action, the drawer displays the fields specific to that action. For the meaning and format of each field, see the OpenCTI API documentation.

    GraphQL actions

    Except for the TAXII 2.1 actions, Get Schema (SDL), and Health Check, every action sends a GraphQL operation. Copy the operation of the action from the GraphQL operations of each action list below, paste it in the GraphQL Query or GraphQL Mutation field. Then fill in the fields of its variables, such as Search or Value. Each field fills the variable of the same name, so keep the variable names when you adapt the operation. An optional field left empty isn't sent. To run an operation no dedicated action covers, use Execute GraphQL Operation and enter the variables as a JSON object in the Variables field.

    The Create Observable action

    The operation of Create Observable creates an IPv4 address. For another observable type, replace the IPv4Addr argument with the one matching the Observable Type field, for example DomainName: {value: $value} for Domain-Name. If an observable with the same value already exists, OpenCTI updates and returns it.

    GraphQL operations of each action

    Each operation matches the placeholder of the GraphQL Query or GraphQL Mutation field of the action.

    Search Entities

    query SearchEntities($search: String!, $first: Int, $types: [String]) {
  stixCoreObjects(search: $search, first: $first, types: $types) {
    edges {
      node {
        id
        standard_id
        entity_type
        representative {
          main
          secondary
        }
        created_at
        updated_at
        objectLabel {
          value
          color
        }
        createdBy {
          ... on Identity {
            name
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

    Search Observables

    query SearchObservables($search: String!, $first: Int) {
  stixCyberObservables(search: $search, first: $first) {
    edges {
      node {
        id
        standard_id
        entity_type
        observable_value
        x_opencti_score
        x_opencti_description
        createdBy {
          ... on Identity {
            name
          }
        }
        objectLabel {
          value
          color
        }
        indicators {
          edges {
            node {
              id
              name
              pattern
              pattern_type
              indicator_types
              x_opencti_score
              confidence
              valid_from
              valid_until
              revoked
              killChainPhases {
                phase_name
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

    Search Indicators

    query SearchIndicators($search: String!, $first: Int) {
  indicators(search: $search, first: $first) {
    edges {
      node {
        id
        standard_id
        name
        pattern
        pattern_type
        indicator_types
        x_opencti_score
        confidence
        valid_from
        valid_until
        revoked
        killChainPhases {
          phase_name
        }
        createdBy {
          ... on Identity {
            name
          }
        }
        objectLabel {
          value
          color
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

    Search Relationships

    query SearchRelationships($fromOrToId: [String], $relationship_type: [String], $first: Int) {
  stixCoreRelationships(
    fromOrToId: $fromOrToId
    relationship_type: $relationship_type
    first: $first
  ) {
    edges {
      node {
        id
        relationship_type
        confidence
        description
        start_time
        stop_time
        from {
          ... on StixCoreObject {
            id
            entity_type
          }
        }
        to {
          ... on StixCoreObject {
            id
            entity_type
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

    Get Observable

    query GetObservable($id: String!) {
  stixCyberObservable(id: $id) {
    id
    standard_id
    entity_type
    observable_value
    x_opencti_score
    x_opencti_description
    created_at
    updated_at
    objectLabel {
      id
      value
      color
    }
    objectMarking {
      id
      definition
      definition_type
    }
    createdBy {
      ... on Identity {
        name
      }
    }
    indicators {
      edges {
        node {
          id
          name
          pattern
          valid_until
          revoked
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

    Create Observable

    mutation CreateObservable($type: String!, $value: String!, $x_opencti_score: Int, $createIndicator: Boolean, $objectLabel: [String], $objectMarking: [String]) {
  stixCyberObservableAdd(
    type: $type
    IPv4Addr: {value: $value}
    x_opencti_score: $x_opencti_score
    createIndicator: $createIndicator
    objectLabel: $objectLabel
    objectMarking: $objectMarking
  ) {
    id
    standard_id
    entity_type
    observable_value
  }
}

    Update Observable Fields

    mutation PatchObservable($id: ID!, $input: [EditInput]!) {
  stixCyberObservableEdit(id: $id) {
    fieldPatch(input: $input) {
      id
      observable_value
      x_opencti_score
      x_opencti_description
    }
  }
}

    Promote Observable to Indicator

    mutation PromoteObservable($id: ID!) {
  stixCyberObservableEdit(id: $id) {
    promoteToIndicator {
      id
      standard_id
      name
      pattern
      pattern_type
      valid_from
      valid_until
    }
  }
}

    Delete Observable

    mutation DeleteObservable($id: ID!) {
  stixCyberObservableEdit(id: $id) {
    delete
  }
}

    Get Indicator

    query GetIndicator($id: String!) {
  indicator(id: $id) {
    id
    standard_id
    name
    description
    pattern
    pattern_type
    indicator_types
    x_opencti_score
    confidence
    valid_from
    valid_until
    revoked
    created_at
    objectLabel {
      id
      value
      color
    }
    objectMarking {
      id
      definition
    }
    killChainPhases {
      kill_chain_name
      phase_name
    }
    createdBy {
      ... on Identity {
        name
      }
    }
    observables {
      edges {
        node {
          id
          entity_type
          observable_value
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

    Create Indicator

    mutation CreateIndicator($input: IndicatorAddInput!) {
  indicatorAdd(input: $input) {
    id
    standard_id
    name
    pattern
    valid_from
    valid_until
  }
}

    Get Entity

    query GetEntity($id: String!) {
  stixCoreObject(id: $id) {
    id
    standard_id
    entity_type
    representative {
      main
      secondary
    }
    created_at
    updated_at
    objectLabel {
      id
      value
      color
    }
    objectMarking {
      id
      definition
      definition_type
    }
    createdBy {
      ... on Identity {
        name
      }
    }
    externalReferences {
      edges {
        node {
          source_name
          url
          external_id
        }
      }
    }
    ... on StixCyberObservable {
      observable_value
    }
  }
}

    Export Entity as STIX

    query GetStix($id: String!) {
  stix(id: $id)
}

    Delete Entity

    mutation DeleteEntity($id: ID!) {
  stixCoreObjectEdit(id: $id) {
    delete
  }
}

    Create Report

    mutation CreateReport($input: ReportAddInput!) {
  reportAdd(input: $input) {
    id
    standard_id
    name
    published
  }
}

    Create Incident

    mutation CreateIncident($input: IncidentAddInput!) {
  incidentAdd(input: $input) {
    id
    standard_id
    name
    first_seen
  }
}

    Create Incident Response Case

    mutation CreateCaseIncident($input: CaseIncidentAddInput!) {
  caseIncidentAdd(input: $input) {
    id
    standard_id
    name
    created
  }
}

    Add Entity to Container

    mutation AddToContainer($id: ID!, $input: StixRefRelationshipAddInput!) {
  containerEdit(id: $id) {
    relationAdd(input: $input) {
      id
    }
  }
}

    Create Relationship

    mutation CreateRelationship($input: StixCoreRelationshipAddInput) {
  stixCoreRelationshipAdd(input: $input) {
    id
    relationship_type
    start_time
    stop_time
  }
}

    Create Sighting

    mutation CreateSighting($input: StixSightingRelationshipAddInput!) {
  stixSightingRelationshipAdd(input: $input) {
    id
    first_seen
    last_seen
    attribute_count
  }
}

    List Labels

    query ListLabels($search: String, $first: Int) {
  labels(search: $search, first: $first) {
    edges {
      node {
        id
        value
        color
      }
    }
  }
}

    Create Label

    mutation CreateLabel($input: LabelAddInput!) {
  labelAdd(input: $input) {
    id
    value
    color
  }
}

    Add Label to Entity

    mutation AddLabel($id: ID!, $input: StixRefRelationshipAddInput!) {
  stixCoreObjectEdit(id: $id) {
    relationAdd(input: $input) {
      id
    }
  }
}

    List Marking Definitions

    query ListMarkings($first: Int) {
  markingDefinitions(first: $first) {
    edges {
      node {
        id
        definition_type
        definition
        x_opencti_order
        x_opencti_color
      }
    }
  }
}

    Add Marking to Entity

    mutation AddMarking($id: ID!, $input: StixRefRelationshipAddInput!) {
  stixCoreObjectEdit(id: $id) {
    relationAdd(input: $input) {
      id
    }
  }
}

    Add Note to Entity

    mutation CreateNote($input: NoteAddInput!) {
  noteAdd(input: $input) {
    id
    standard_id
    attribute_abstract
    content
    created
  }
}

    List Connectors

    query ListConnectors {
  connectors {
    id
    name
    active
    auto
    connector_type
    connector_scope
    connector_state
    updated_at
  }
}

    List Enrichment Connectors for Type

    query EnrichmentConnectors($type: String!) {
  enrichmentConnectors(type: $type) {
    id
    name
    active
    connector_scope
  }
}

    Ask Enrichment

    mutation AskEnrichment($id: ID!, $connectorId: ID!) {
  stixCoreObjectEdit(id: $id) {
    askEnrichment(connectorId: $connectorId) {
      id
      name
      status
    }
  }
}

    Introspect Types

    query IntrospectType($name: String!) {
  __type(name: $name) {
    name
    kind
    fields(includeDeprecated: false) {
      name
      type {
        name
        kind
        ofType {
          name
          kind
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

    Get Relationship Mapping

    query RelationshipsMapping {
  schemaRelationsTypesMapping {
    key
    values
  }
}

    Who Am I

    query Me {
  me {
    id
    name
    user_email
    firstname
    lastname
    capabilities {
      name
    }
    objectOrganization {
      edges {
        node {
          id
          name
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

    Get Platform Info

    query About {
  about {
    version
    dependencies {
      name
      version
    }
  }
}

    Failed operations return a 200 status code

    OpenCTI answers a failed GraphQL operation, for example because of an invalid token, an invalid input, or a missing right, with a 200 status code and an errors array in the response body. The node then succeeds. Check body.errors in a later node, for example with an If flow node.

    - Editor mode

    For actions that send a request body, select how to provide it:

    • Form: Fill in one field per body parameter.
    • Raw: Provide the whole request body in the Request body (raw) field.

    - Query parameters

    Query parameters sent with the request, entered as key-value pairs. Select to add a parameter. This section appears only for actions that accept query parameters.

  7. Optional: Configure the following settings.

    - Proxy

    Configure how the node connects to the external service when a proxy is required.

    Select a Proxy mode:

    • Do not use a proxy: No proxy is applied. All requests are sent directly. This is the default.

    • Use the platform default proxy configuration: Uses the global proxy settings defined in TheHive application.conf. See proxy configuration in TheHive.

    • Configure a custom proxy: Defines a custom proxy for this node, overriding the global configuration.

A Wazuh integration node runs operations against the Wazuh server API. It can list, add, restart, and delete agents, assign agents to groups, run active responses, and run file integrity monitoring scans. It can also read file integrity monitoring findings, security configuration assessment results, rules, CDB lists, manager status and logs, and task status. Each operation is a dedicated action selected within the node.

  2. Select a workflow from the list.

  3. Drag the previous node connector to an empty area of the canvas.

  4. In the What is the next step? drawer, select Integrations.

    • $<node_name>.body.results[0].id: Reads the first identifier of an API response.
    • $<node_name>.body.items | map(.name) | join(", "): Turns a list of objects into a comma-separated text.
    • $<node_name>.body.createdAt / 1000 | todate: Formats a TheHive date, a Unix timestamp in milliseconds, as an ISO 8601 date.
    • $<node_name>.output.title | ascii_upcase: Converts a text to uppercase.

    See Jq Functions for the full list of available functions.

    Fields marked with * are mandatory.

    - Base URL *

    The URL of your Wazuh server API, for example https://<wazuh_server>:55000.

    - Authentication *

    In the Authentication section, select the Authentication method and provide its credentials. The Wazuh node supports two methods:

    Authentication method Fields basic_auth Username *, Password bearer_token Bearer token *

    The Wazuh server API accepts a username and password only to issue a token. Use basic_auth with the Authenticate action, and bearer_token with every other action. In the Bearer token field, insert the body.data.token output of the Authenticate node with the $var button. By default, a token expires after 900 seconds. Reference secret global variables instead of pasting credentials directly.

    - Headers

    Extra headers added to every request sent by the node. Select to add a header key and its value.

    Header values are stored in plaintext

    Header values appear in plaintext in the workflow execution history. Reference a secret global variable instead of pasting a credential directly.

    - Action *

    The operation to perform in Wazuh. Available actions:

    Family Actions Authentication Authenticate Agents List Agents, Add Agent, Insert Agent with ID and Key, Delete Agents, Get Agent Key, Restart Agent, Get Agents Status Summary, Assign Agent to Group Active Response Run Active Response File Integrity Monitoring Get FIM Findings, Run FIM Scan Security Configuration Assessment Get SCA Results, Get SCA Policy Checks Rules Get Rules CDB Lists Get CDB Lists, Get CDB List File Manager Get Manager Status, Get Manager Logs Tasks List Tasks Status

    After you select an action, the drawer displays the fields specific to that action. For the meaning and format of each field, see the Wazuh server API reference.

    The Run Active Response action

    The Command field takes the name of a command declared in a <command> block of the manager ossec.conf file. To call an active response script by its file name instead, prefix it with !, for example !firewall-drop. Enter the target IP address in the Source IP field for firewall-drop, host-deny, route-null, and netsh, and the target user account in the Target User field for disable-account.

    Failures on agents return a 200 status code

    - Editor mode

    For actions that send a request body, select how to provide it:

    • Form: Fill in one field per body parameter.
    • Raw: Provide the whole request body in the Request body (raw) field.

    - Query parameters

    Query parameters sent with the request, entered as key-value pairs. Select to add a parameter. This section appears only for actions that accept query parameters.

docs.title: Configure a Set local variable node
docs.text:
A Set local variable node creates one or more local variables during workflow execution. It doesn't modify existing ones. If two nodes declare a variable with the same name, both coexist and are each referenced by their node name. Variables accumulate in the workflow context as execution progresses.

To update a value, add a new Set local variable node downstream with the desired variable name, and reference the earlier value.

Global variables

To reuse the same values across multiple workflows, create global variables from the Global variables tab in the Flow view. These values are defined at the organization level and can't be modified within workflows.

  1. Go to the Flow view from the sidebar menu.

  2. Select a workflow from the list.

  3. Drag the previous node connector to an empty area of the canvas.

  4. In the What is the next step? drawer, select Transformations.

  5. Select Set local variable.

  6. Select in the Variables section.

  7. In the Set local variable drawer, enter the following information:

    Fields marked with * are mandatory.

    - Name *

    The identifier for the variable.

    - Type *

    The data type of the variable: string, number, boolean, array, or json.

    - Value *

    The value assigned to the variable.

    Supported formats include:

    • Static values
    • References to other variables, using the $var button
    • jq expressions, using the functions listed in Jq Functions

    Variables

    Insert a variable with the $var button, or enter $ and select a variable from the suggestions. To access a field, select the variable to edit its jq expression, or use the + button to insert the variable and the field together.

    Inside the expression, jq functions transform the value before it's inserted in the field. The whole expression stays inside the blue reference, for example:

    • $<node_name>.body.results[0].id: Reads the first identifier of an API response.
    • $<node_name>.body.items | map(.name) | join(", "): Turns a list of objects into a comma-separated text.
    • $<node_name>.body.createdAt / 1000 | todate: Formats a TheHive date, a Unix timestamp in milliseconds, as an ISO 8601 date.
    • $<node_name>.output.title | ascii_upcase: Converts a text to uppercase.

    See Jq Functions for the full list of available functions.

    Secret global variables

    The value can't reference a secret global variable because the resolved value would appear in plain text in the execution logs.

    Use an online jq playground to validate your expressions before adding them to the workflow.

    Examples

    • "Case $caseNumber – severity $caseSeverity": Builds a text from two variables.
    • if $caseSeverity >= 3 then "High" else "Low" end: Maps a numeric severity to a label.
    • {number: $caseNumber, assignee: $caseAssignee, title: $caseTitle}: Builds a JSON object from several variables.
    • $caseTitle | ascii_downcase | gsub("[^a-z0-9]+"; "-"): Turns a title into a lowercase identifier such as suspicious-login-from-new-country, for a ticket or file name.
    • $caseObservables | map(select(.dataType == "domain") | .data) | unique | join(", "): Lists the distinct domain observables as a comma-separated text.
    • $caseTags | map(select(startswith("mitre:")) | ltrimstr("mitre:")): Extracts the MITRE ATT&CK technique identifiers from tags such as mitre:T1566.
    • $caseCreatedAt / 1000 | strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"): Formats a TheHive date, a Unix timestamp in milliseconds, as a readable date.
    • $httpResponse.body | fromjson | .results[0].score // 0: Parses a JSON text returned by an API and reads a score, defaulting to 0 when missing.
    • {id: $caseNumber, iocs: ($caseObservables | map(.data)), created: ($caseCreatedAt / 1000 | todate)}: Builds the payload of an outgoing webhook from several variables.

    You can select to add multiple variables in the same node.

  8. Optional: Select Add options to configure the following settings.

    - Timeout & retry

    Configure how the node handles execution time limits and failure recovery.

    If the timeout is reached, the node fails.

    Global timeout vs. local timeout

    A timeout for the entire workflow is defined when creating the workflow. When both a node timeout and a workflow-level timeout are defined, the shortest timeout value applies.

    Field Description Timeout Maximum allowed execution time for the node, in seconds, minutes, or hours. The minimum value is 30 seconds. Retry attempts Number of times the node is retried on failure. Retry delay Time to wait between retry attempts, in seconds, minutes, or hours. Without a delay, retries run 1 second apart by default. Backoff Coefficient applied to the retry delay to increase the wait time after each failed attempt.

    Retries and timeouts

    If the node includes retry settings, the timeout applies to each attempt, not to the total duration of all attempts.

    - Execution configuration

    Set the Execution mode to control how the node behaves when several branches converge on it.

    Mode Behavior Execute once per branch The node runs once for each incoming branch. Applies when this section isn't configured. Wait for all branches The node waits for all incoming branches to complete, then runs once.

Execution output

When executed, the node returns the value assigned to the variable as the output.

To access the output, select your Set local variable node and then select in the top-right corner of the screen. Hover over the output name to view its details.

This output can then be reused as an output variable in subsequent nodes, using the $var button or by entering $ and selecting the variable from the suggestions. The inserted reference is displayed as $<node_name>.<field_name>.

docs.title: Configure a Python code node
docs.text:
A Python code node executes custom Python scripts within a workflow. Use it for advanced data transformations, integration with external tools, or any logic that standard nodes can't handle.

  1. Go to the Flow view from the sidebar menu.

  2. Select a workflow from the list.

  3. Drag the previous node connector to an empty area of the canvas.

  4. In the What is the next step? drawer, select Transformations.

  5. Select Python code.

  6. In the Python code drawer, enter your Python script in the editor.

    • You can use libraries available in the configured execution image. The default image ships the Python standard library only. Providing additional libraries requires a custom execution image configured on the deployment.
    • You can use variables.
    • Under Environment, you can define environment variables the script can read. Each value can reference a variable.

    Using variables in Python scripts

    To insert a variable, use the $var button and assign it to a variable in your script:

    <var_name> = $<var>

    The $<var> reference is stored as a flow.get("<variable>") call. To get a value when the variable is missing, pass it as a second argument: flow.get("<variable>", <fallback_value>).

    Variables are scoped to the script by default. To make a value available to the workflow and reuse it as an output variable in later nodes, you must explicitly return it as a workflow output using flow.set():

    flow.set("<var_name>", <var_name>)

    For values stored as files, such as large or binary content, use flow.get_file_path() and flow.set_file_from_path(). These functions hand you a file path to read from or write to, instead of loading the whole value into the script.

    • flow.get_file_path("<variable>") returns the path of a file made available to the script for a variable holding a file reference. Read it with normal file operations.
    • flow.set_file_from_path("<name>", "<path>") registers a file written by the script as an output variable. The file is stored after the run, and the output carries its file reference.

    See Examples for real-world use cases.

    Accessing a field from a variable

    To access a field, enter .<field_name> directly after the variable.

    Only run code you trust

    The script is executed as is on the server, with the same trust as the person who wrote it. Unlike the other nodes, the script has no network restrictions: it can reach any system the server can, including your internal network. Only paste code you understand, and review the code nodes of any imported workflow before running it.

    A secret variable the script reads is handed to it in clear. Anything the script prints ends up in its script_out output and in the execution logs, so never print a secret.

  7. Optional: Select Add options to configure the following settings.

    - Timeout & retry

    Configure how the node handles execution time limits and failure recovery.

    If the timeout is reached, the node fails.

    Global timeout vs. local timeout

    A timeout for the entire workflow is defined when creating the workflow. When both a node timeout and a workflow-level timeout are defined, the shortest timeout value applies.

    Field Description Timeout Maximum allowed execution time for the node, in seconds, minutes, or hours. The minimum value is 30 seconds. Retry attempts Number of times the node is retried on failure. Retry delay Time to wait between retry attempts, in seconds, minutes, or hours. Without a delay, retries run 1 second apart by default. Backoff Coefficient applied to the retry delay to increase the wait time after each failed attempt.

    Retries and timeouts

    If the node includes retry settings, the timeout applies to each attempt, not to the total duration of all attempts.

    - Execution configuration

    Set the Execution mode to control how the node behaves when several branches converge on it.

    Mode Behavior Execute once per branch The node runs once for each incoming branch. Applies when this section isn't configured. Wait for all branches The node waits for all incoming branches to complete, then runs once.

Execution outputs

When executed, the node returns the following outputs. Each output is a JSON value:

Output Type Description script_out string The raw output returned by the script. script_code number The exit code returned by the script. 0 indicates success. script_image string The Docker image digest used to run the script. custom output any Any additional outputs defined using flow.set().

To access outputs, select your Python code node and then select in the top-right corner of the screen. Hover over each output name to view its details.

These outputs can then be reused as output variables in subsequent nodes, using the $var button or by entering $ and selecting the output from the suggestions. Inserted references are displayed in the following form:

  • $<node_name>.script_out: to get the raw script output
  • $<node_name>.script_code: to get the exit code
  • $<node_name>.script_image: to get the Docker image digest used to run the script
  • $<node_name>.<custom_output>: to get a value you exposed with flow.set()

docs.text: The following examples show common use cases for the Python code node.

docs.title: Multi-criteria alert scoring
docs.text:
Calculates a priority score from 0 to 100 and a priority level from P1 to P4, based on severity, asset criticality, and enrichment results.

severity = $severity
asset_criticality = $asset_criticality
vt_verdict = $vt_verdict
ioc_matched = $ioc_matched

severity_scores = {"low": 10, "medium": 30, "high": 60, "critical": 90}
score = severity_scores.get(severity, 0)
score += min(int(asset_criticality or 1) * 5, 25)
if vt_verdict == "malicious":
    score += 40
if ioc_matched:
    score += 30
score = min(score, 100)
priority = "P1" if score >= 80 else "P2" if score >= 60 else "P3" if score >= 40 else "P4"
flow.set("score", score)
flow.set("priority", priority)

docs.title: SIEM/EDR payload normalization
docs.text:
Maps source-specific field names from SIEM or EDR payloads to a consistent set of output fields, regardless of the source system.

source_type = $source_type
raw_payload = $raw_payload

mapping = {
    "siem": ("SourceIP", "UserName", "ComputerName"),
    "edr":  ("local_ip", "user_name", "device_name")
}

ip_k, user_k, host_k = mapping.get(source_type, ("src_ip", "user", "hostname"))

src_ip = raw_payload.get(ip_k, "")
user = raw_payload.get(user_k, "")
hostname = raw_payload.get(host_k, "")

flow.set("src_ip", src_ip)
flow.set("user", user)
flow.set("hostname", hostname)
